newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Disney Q4 results climb.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Disney Q4 results climb.

text.p: Walt Disney Co Tuesday reported fourth-quarter net earnings per share jumped 63 percent as theme parks and resorts results reflected record attendance levels.
A full text of its statement follows.
BURBANK, Calif., Nov. 26 /PRNewswire/ -- The Walt Disney Company (NYSE: DIS) today reported operating results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 1996.

"I am extremely pleased with the progress we have made in integrating Disney and ABC," said Michael D. Eisner, chairman and CEO. "The fact that we continued our strong growth during this period proves that the combined operations are working and working well."

Disney President Michael S. Ovitz said, "The performance of Disney theme parks, all of which set new attendance records for the fiscal year, was the highlight of a very successful 12 months. We look for continued growth and leadership in this area as work moves forward on three new parks which we are currently developing."

The following discussion of pro forma and as reported operating results excludes the impact of two non-recurring charges, described below, which were recorded by the Company during the second quarter. To enhance comparability, the pro forma results assume the acquisition of ABC occurred at the beginning of the respective periods for which information is presented.

Pro forma revenues for the quarter increased 12% to $5.3 billion and operating income increased 27% to $858 million. Net income for the quarter increased 60% to $354 million and earnings per share increased 63% to $0.52. Revenues for the fiscal year increased 12% to $21.2 billion and operating income increased 7% to $3.7 billion. Net income for the fiscal year increased 16% to $1.5 billion, and earnings per share increased 15% to $2.23. The quarter and fiscal year pro forma information reflect a full period of operating results for both The Walt Disney Company and ABC, and a full period impact of amortization of intangible assets, interest expense, the new effective income tax rate and additional shares outstanding related to the acquisition.

Creative Content pro forma revenues for the quarter increased 18% to $2.7 billion and operating income increased 31% to $387 million. For the fiscal year, revenues increased 17% to $10.5 billion while operating income at $1.6 billion approximated prior-year levels.

Creative Content results for the quarter reflected the successful domestic home video releases of "Oliver & Company" and "Aladdin and the King of Thieves," the domestic box office success of "Phenomenon" and the strong international theatrical performances of "The Rock" and "The Hunchback of Notre Dame." Results for the quarter also reflected growth in international consumer products licensing. These increases were partially offset by lower television results due to the syndication of "Home Improvement" in the prior year. Results for the fiscal year reflected the domestic home video success of "Cinderella," "Pocahontas" and "The Aristocats," the international home video performances of "The Lion King" and "101 Dalmatians," and continued worldwide growth in consumer products licensing. Results for the year also reflected the successful performance of various live-action titles in the home video and pay TV markets, including "The Santa Clause," "While You Were Sleeping" and "Crimson Tide" as well as the worldwide theatrical success of "Toy Story." These results were offset by lower domestic theatrical film performances, the write-off of certain development projects during the second quarter, and difficult comparisons to the prior-year period, which benefited from "The Lion King" in the worldwide home video and international theatrical markets, and "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs" in worldwide home video.

Broadcasting pro forma revenues increased 4% to $1.4 billion for the quarter and operating income increased 36% to $229 million. For the fiscal year, revenues increased 4% to $6.2 billion and operating income increased 12% to $1.1 billion.

Broadcasting results for the quarter and fiscal year benefited from significant reductions in program amortization and other costs attributable to the acquisition, primarily at the television network. These reductions exceeded the impact of ratings deterioration on revenues at the television network. The fiscal year results also reflect strong increases in advertising and affiliate revenues at ESPN.

Theme Parks and Resorts revenues for the quarter increased 11% to $1.2 billion and operating income grew 16% to $242 million. For the fiscal year, revenues increased 13% to $4.5 billion and operating income rose 15% to $990 million.

Theme Parks and Resorts results for the quarter and fiscal year reflected record attendance levels, exceeding the record attendance achieved in the prior year, and increased guest spending at Walt Disney World and Disneyland. Attendance gains reflected increased domestic and international tourist visitation, including the response to the Main Street Electrical Parade farewell at Disneyland. In addition, increased occupied room nights and guest spending at Florida resorts contributed to these results.

On an as reported basis, reflecting ABC's results from the effective date of the acquisition (February 9, 1996), revenues for the quarter increased 69% to $5.3 billion and operating income rose 73% to $858 million. Net income increased 27% to $336 million and earnings per share decreased 2% to $0.49. For the fiscal year, revenues increased 54% to $18.7 billion, operating income rose 35% to $3.3 billion, net income increased 11% to $1.5 billion and earnings per share decreased 5% to $2.48.
These as reported results reflect significant increases in amortization of intangible assets, interest expense, the effective income tax rate and shares outstanding for 1996 due to the acquisition.

As noted above, the Company recorded two non-recurring charges during the second quarter. The Company recognized a $300 million non-cash charge related to the implementation of Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 121, and recognized a $225 million charge for costs related to the acquisition of ABC. For the fiscal year, these items reduced as reported net income from $1.5 billion to $1.2 billion and earnings per share from $2.48 to $1.96.

During the quarter, the Company repurchased 8.2 million of its shares at an average price of $56.53 per share for a total cost of $462 million. The share repurchases were made under the Company's existing stock repurchase program.
